A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title and TPO-to-TPR renaming. All pages, including appendices, were readable; matching methods, tables and qualitative examples support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, feedback-quality assessments, scaling experiments and qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds curriculum, cross-architecture, cost and hallucination-type evaluations.

M1.justification: v1 uses greedy highest/lowest-scoring topic replacements followed by DPO. v3 retains this as TPR and introduces TPR-CL, with iterative reference-model updates and progressively harder rejected alternatives (Section 3.4, Appendix B). It also assigns decomposition, question conversion and textual consistency checking to the reference model instead of v1's supplementary LLaMA-3 model.

E1.justification: The seven training-data sources and five original evaluation benchmarks are retained. v3 adds POPE's object-existence probes under different sampling strategies and RefoMB's image-based hallucination and reasoning evaluation (Table 1, Appendix E.2). This extends coverage within the existing visual hallucination domain.

E2.justification: v3 adds FGAIF to the main comparison, expands comparisons with whole-response ranking and external rewriting strategies, and introduces naive RLAIF in the Qwen comparison (Tables 1, 2 and 4). Its cost analysis also evaluates GPT-4V rewriting against TPR and RLAIF-V. v1's separately identified OmniLMM consistency comparison is removed.

E3.justification: The stated preference-data total changes from 21k to 20k; TPR-CL introduces 12k warm-up and 8k hard-mining instances with iterative training. v3 adds Qwen-VL-2B experiments and removes the LoRA evaluation. Overall response-quality assessment changes from multiway GPT-4V selections to pairwise win rates against GPT-4V responses. These reported changes do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds random-replacement ablations, external-versus-intrinsic hallucination distributions, curriculum benefits by hallucination type, monetary cost comparisons and cross-architecture generalization tests. It also adds curriculum-generated rejected responses to retained qualitative examples. Earlier candidate-generation and clustering ablations are largely retained through merging or relocation.

E5.justification: v1 Section 3.1.1 explicitly specifies different random seeds for generating candidate responses; v3 retains ten candidates but omits that seed statement. This is a limited seed-documentation change, not evidence of changed experimental replication. Neither version reports confidence intervals, repeated-training-run uncertainty or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original greedy and self-labeling scores largely recur in v3, which adds TPR-CL results, including ObjectHal scores of 3.4/1.8, and new benchmark, Qwen, curation and cost results. LoRA results are removed. The no-in-context-rewriting ablation changes from 8.0/3.9 in v1 Table 5 to 35.5/20.1 in v3 Table 2; the latter matches v1's differently described OmniLMM experiment, leaving its provenance unclear.

T1.justification: v3 explicitly defines the reward gap as r(yw; x) minus r(yl; x) and connects preference learning to Bradley-Terry modeling; v1 discusses the gap informally. The existing clustering predicates are retained under revised notation in Appendix A. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from scalable self-correction through enlarged preference contrasts to systematic control of reward-gap configuration. v3 elevates curriculum-based hard-negative mining and superior data efficiency into explicit abstract and introduction claims, substantially expanding the contribution beyond the retained greedy method.

C2.justification: v3 argues that maximizing reward gaps can neglect subtle errors and that external rewriting can introduce hallucination patterns unlike the target model's failures. It interprets curriculum gains through quantities and spatial-relation errors. Its limitations replace v1's rudimentary resampling/clustering concern with boundaries involving complex multimodal reasoning and further curation strategies.

D1.justification: v3 documents curriculum stages and selection percentiles, specifies CLIP/Pearson-correlation and Louvain-style clustering details, and discloses the 8k ablation subset. v1's future-release promise becomes a project address and Appendix H's description of supplementary code.zip, setup, curation, training and evaluation scripts. The PDFs establish these access disclosures, but do not verify the referenced artifacts.

R1.justification: Research positioning is substantially rewritten around ranking versus rewriting and their ability to configure reward gaps. Newly cited Bradley-Terry, RS-DPO and beta-DPO work supports this central framing, alongside expanded discussion of hallucination causes and newer models. This exceeds bibliographic updates to retained references.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten, with TPO/MLLM terminology becoming TPR/VLM. Clustering formalism moves into Appendix A, and the appendices are reorganized into dedicated curriculum, cost, implementation, impacts and reproducibility sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout and substantially redraws the method diagrams. Ablation tables are consolidated with colored configuration differences, quality pie charts are replaced by bar-chart presentations, and curriculum and cost plots are added. Retained clustering and qualitative displays are relocated or reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through a second architecture, broader curation comparisons and targeted curriculum analyses, while providing more implementation information. However, the unexplained reassignment of the 35.5/20.1 ablation results and changed training-budget description limit confidence in parts of the revised evidence. These tradeoffs support a modest overall improvement rather than a clear substantial gain.
